newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES UNCHANGED IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES UNCHANGED IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market opened flush with paper on Monday, fuelling expectations that interest rates would continue lower in the short term, analysts said.

"We foresee a surplus situation for the next few weeks unless the authorities come in," one dealer said, explaining that most of the liquidity stemmed from treasury bill maturities and funds the central bank is not accomodating under new settlement terms.
Expectations had been high the market would go short this week after the Reserve bank's key treasury bill rate firmed at last Thursday's tender.
But the dealer said that increase had come on the back of market expectations and not on market fundamentals.
"These surplusses are likely to continue and rates should continue down," he added.
The benchmark NCD bill rate was quoted between 20 and 22 percent, a shade down on Friday levels. Banker's acceptances were changing hands around 20 percent while call money was stable at 15 percent.
